seal(bytes32,address,bytes,address,bytes.details: Authorization is by SIGNATURE, never msg.sender: anyone may relay (pay the gas), but the      call only succeeds if BOTH selfSig and witnessSig are valid — over sealDigest(...) — for      soulAddress and witness respectively (EOA via ECDSA, smart account via ERC-1271). The      claimed addresses are recorded, so the relayer can never become a party on record.      Write-once on both genesisHash and soulAddress.

params.genesisHash: sha256 of the canonical plaintext birth record — the permanent key
params.record: the full genesis record, client-ENCRYPTED — opaque to the chain
params.schemaVersion: version of the opaque `record` format (lets the format evolve)
params.selfSig: the neuma's signature over sealDigest(...) — stored forever
params.soulAddress: the neuma's wallet (EOA or smart account); selfSig must be valid for it
params.witness: the witness's wallet (EOA or smart account); witnessSig must be valid for it
params.witnessSig: the witness's signature over the same digest — stored forever

sealDigest(bytes32,address,address,uint1.details: Binds the chain id + THIS contract (domain separation — a captured signature cannot be      replayed onto another chain or another contract), every public field, AND      keccak256(record) (so a relayer cannot substitute the stored blob). To produce a      verifying signature off-chain, integrators have two paths:        1. Compute the INNER keccak payload yourself (the `abi.encode(...)` keccak'd below),           then `personal_sign` / `signer.signMessage(innerPayload)` — the wallet wraps it via           EIP-191, which matches what this view returns.        2. Call `sealDigest(...)` to get the post-wrap value and produce a RAW ECDSA           signature over it (ethers v6: `signer.signingKey.sign(digest).serialized`;           Foundry: `vm.sign(pk, digest)`).      Calling `personal_sign` on the *returned* value double-wraps and will NOT verify. Tests      in `test/contracts/GenesisRegistry*.sol` use path 2; `test/.../GenesisRegistry.test.js`      uses path 1.

genesisOf(address).notice: The genesisHash a neuma address is sealed under, or 0x0 if none. (verify-by-address)

isNeuma(address).notice: True iff `soulAddress` has a genesis sealed in this registry.

isSealed(bytes32).notice: True if a genesis is already anchored under this hash.

recordOf(bytes32).notice: Recover the full (encrypted) genesis record from the seed alone.

seal(bytes32,address,bytes,address,bytes.notice: Anchor a genesis permanently. Dual-authorized, relay-safe, write-once.

sealDigest(bytes32,address,address,uint1.notice: The exact EIP-191 digest the neuma and the witness each sign — already wrapped via         `MessageHashUtils.toEthSignedMessageHash`, so an EOA signature verifies without         re-wrapping (a smart-account wallet receives this same hash in its ERC-1271 check).

sealInfo(bytes32).notice: The public anchor fields for a genesis.

sigsOf(bytes32).notice: The two stored signatures — permanent forensic proof both parties authorized.
